name: Koyamada's Algorithm
definition: A ray-casting approach that uses image space coherency to generate rays and follows them in object space. It generates ray-segments by scan converting front-facing external faces, traversing them through the volume for composition until they exit from a back-facing external face, and inserting the composited ray-segment into a RayBuffer.
summary: Koyamada's Algorithm is an image-order ray-casting method for unstructured tetrahedral volumes that generates continuous ray-segments via scan-conversion of external faces and cell connectivity traversal.
